newsitem.title: CHINA: China inflation seen at 6.5 percent in 1996 - Zhu.
newsitem.headline: China inflation seen at 6.5 percent in 1996 - Zhu.

text.p: China's fight against inflation has produced better than expected results and retail price rises should be held within 6.5 percent this year, Vice Premier Zhu Rongji said on Wednesday.

Zhu, China's top economic policymaker, also repeated earlier forecasts that economic growth would be about 10 percent in 1996 and foreign exchange reserves would top $100 billion by the end of the year.
The forecasts, made at an international business forum, were largely in line with previous estimates.

Central bank governor Dai Xianglong said that retail price inflation would be held to less than 6.6 percent and economic growth would be nine to 10 percent. Foreign exchange reserves were $95.363 billion at the end of September.

"This year the situation of China's economic development is pretty good," Zhu told the meeting. "The macro-economic situation has been further improved, the adjustment of the economic structure has been strengthened and inflation has been brought under control much more effectively than expected."
Zhu said that over the next 15 years, the economy was expected to maintain healthy growth with an annual increase of 8.9 percent.
